headline.caveat: initial AI-ready data-center capacity from TCS HyperVault, with a stated path/option to scale to 1GW; contract dollars undisclosed

realized_to_date.caveat: capacity being built; no payments quantified publicly

nature_md: Announced Feb 19, 2026 at the India AI Impact Summit: OpenAI becomes the **first customer** of Tata Consultancy Services' HyperVault data-center business, anchoring 100MW of AI-ready capacity in India with ambitions to scale to 1GW, as part of OpenAI's Stargate-branded international buildout ('OpenAI for India'). The capacity lets OpenAI's frontier models run in-country for latency, data-residency, and government/mission-critical compliance. The partnership is two-way: Tata also deploys ChatGPT Enterprise across its workforce and standardizes on OpenAI tooling for AI-native software development (a smaller reverse flow, dollars undisclosed).

accounting.payer_treatment_md: OpenAI pays for capacity as delivered (structure — lease vs. managed service — undisclosed). India is a top-2 ChatGPT market by users but monetizes far below US rates, so this is margin-dilutive capacity bought for strategic position.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Anchor-tenant revenue that launches TCS's HyperVault line; Tata carries the buildout capex. For Tata the risk is classic anchor-tenant concentration: HyperVault's initial economics depend on one foreign counterparty.

events.title: OpenAI anchors TCS HyperVault with 100MW, eyeing 1GW (Stargate India)
